headline: Waymo recalls all 3,791 U.S. robotaxis after autonomous vehicle drives into San Antonio floodwaters — one Waymo drove straight into a flooded high-speed road; OTA software fix deployed fleet-wide; recall highlights weather-edge-case perception failures as an industry-wide AV risk; Tesla faces the same challenge but benefits from competitor's public safety scrutiny shifting regulatory attention; incident follows Reuters investigation into Tesla's own robotaxi availability constraints published same day (Reuters / Electrek / Bloomberg)

TSLA falls ~4% on May 12 as hotter-than-expected US inflation print triggers broad tech selloff — macro headwind, not a fundamental break; CPI data signals higher-for-longer rate environment pressuring high-multiple growth stocks; TSLA retreats from ~$461 intraday high despite China FSD thesis intact; Invezz: 'selloff is macro-driven; key near-term driver remains the May 13–15 Beijing visit and push for Full Self-Driving approval'; TSLA still up ~15% over prior five sessions (Invezz / Yahoo Finance)

Barclays initiates TSLA with Hold rating — joins bulge-bracket consensus view that current valuation adequately reflects near-term robotaxi and FSD optionality; sell-side now spans JPMorgan Underweight ($145 PT) to Piper Sandler Bull ($500 PT) with consensus Hold near ~$400; key re-rating triggers cited: China FSD regulatory approval, Cybercab ramp velocity, and Q2 2026 delivery acceleration; Barclays note arrives as TSLA trades near 52-week highs following trade-summit-driven rally (TipRanks)

TSLA surges ~3.7% to ~$461 as US-China trade talks spark broad market rally — Trump delegation (including Musk) arrives in Beijing for May 13–15 summit with Xi Jinping; investors pricing in potential trade normalization that could fast-track Tesla's China FSD approval, reduce tariff headwinds on Giga Shanghai exports, and improve broader EV market conditions; Piper Sandler (Alex Potter) simultaneously reiterates $500 PT stating 'at ~$400/share, investors get Optimus for free' — EV + energy businesses alone justify ~$400/share, making robotics and AI inference pure optionality; TSLA up ~15% in five sessions through May 12 (CNN / Piper Sandler / TipRanks)

Reuters investigation: Tesla robotaxi faces Texas-sized wait times and safety bottleneck — ~50 vehicles in Austin vs Waymo's 250+; Dallas reporter spent 2 hours on a 20-min trip (avoided main expressway, surface streets only); Houston app canceled bookings with no car available for 30+ min; Austin: zero cars available in 27% of checks, 15+ min waits half the time; Electrek argues 'convenience issues' mask the real constraint — Musk admitted on Q1 earnings call that SAFETY validation is what limits fleet expansion, not operations; 25 total unsupervised vehicles across all three Texas cities (Reuters / Electrek)

TSLA slips ~2% premarket as Musk joins Trump's China delegation (May 13–15) — Elon Musk confirmed in Beijing party alongside Apple CEO Tim Cook, BlackRock CEO Larry Fink, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, and others; Tesla's China FSD approval has slipped from Q2 to Q3 2026 target after Musk suggested Feb/Mar timing last year; diplomatic access to Chinese leadership viewed as potential near-term unlock for Tesla's largest untapped FSD market; TSLA closed at $445 on May 11 (+3.89%) and is ripping above its 200-day moving average (BBC / Stocktwits / NDTV Profit)

Tesla FSD gains new European foothold — Ireland's Department of Transport confirms active engagement with Tesla and the National Standards Authority of Ireland (NSAI) ahead of potential FSD Supervised approval; follows Netherlands (April 10) and Sweden (April 27) greenlights; Tesla targeting broader EU deployment 'as early as summer 2026'; harmonized EU-wide clearance requires 15/27 member states — next Technical Committee vote: July 2026 (Teslarati / RTE)

Austin robotaxi fleet: 50 active rider vehicles + 38 Cybercabs in test fleet; unsupervised ride rate hits 66.7% — 28 of 42 rides in last 7 days with no safety driver; up from 59.0% on May 8 and 27.8% on May 6; fleet now operating unsupervised during evening hours for first time as of May 4; pace of autonomous operational maturity accelerating sharply across both daytime and night sessions (robotaxitracker.com / Teslarati)

TSLA closes at $445 on May 11 (+3.89%) — stock ripping above 200-day moving average; +33% off the post-earnings $373 low set Apr 23; +12.6% YTD; approaching $450–$460 resistance zone; Piper Sandler (Alex Potter) reiterates that Tesla's core EV and energy businesses justify ~$400/share alone, making Optimus, robotaxi, and AI inference 'essentially free' optionality at current prices; bull case reinforced by accelerating Austin robotaxi unsupervised rate and Cybercab production ramp (Yahoo Finance / IBTimes)

Tesla China retail sales fell 10% YoY in April to 25,956 units — domestic sales fell 15% YoY; the widely reported '+36% April surge' was wholesale/export output from Giga Shanghai including European and APAC exports, NOT Chinese consumer purchases; Q1 2026 China retail crashed 16% YoY with January alone down 45%; Tesla now risks falling behind Xiaomi in China market share by end of 2026 as domestic BEV market grew +2.4% YoY in April; bear signal for the China delivery recovery thesis (Electrek / CnEVPost)
